name: showreel-28-thumb

voice.text: Why does your thumb hit the wrong link? Your links are tiny, so one tap covers two: you aim for Archive, and get Delete. The fix: min height, forty four pixels. Now every tap lands where you aim.

caption:
Why does your thumb hit the wrong link? 👍

Menu links set in small text are often only about 16 px tall, so one fingertip covers two of them: you aim for Archive and get Delete. Give each link a real target: display: block and min-height: 44px. The text keeps its size; only the area you can tap grows. WCAG asks for targets of at least 24 × 24 CSS px (2.5.8, AA) and 44 × 44 for the best level (2.5.5, AAA). Works in every browser.
Save it for your next menu or footer, or send it to whoever builds your app.

sources.note: MDN, Understanding WCAG, Operable: 2.5.5 Target Size (AAA) at least 44 CSS px wide and tall; 2.5.8 Target size minimum (AA) at least 24 x 24 px, with spacing exceptions
MDN min-height: sets the minimum height of an element; applies to all elements but non-replaced inline elements (hence display: block on the link)

tip.title: Why does your thumb hit the wrong link?
tip.why: Links set in small text are only as tall as their line, about 16 px, so one fingertip covers two of them. A block link with min-height: 44px gets a real target while its text keeps its size. WCAG asks for at least 24 x 24 CSS px (2.5.8, AA) and 44 x 44 for AAA (2.5.5), per MDN's Understanding WCAG.
